label.explanation: msg-895290 at partition 0 offset 721265 contains bytes event-processor cannot parse. It is nacked and redelivered forever because no max-retries/DLQ is configured (lines 210, 211, 223, 224, 244, 245, 248, 249, 271, 272). That message blocks its partition, so lag grows (lines 235, 256, 270, 281, 296, 305, 319, 331, 346, 356, 375, 387) and downstream work stalls (lines 259, 285, 303, 330, 349, 378). The consumer has capacity — it's stuck on one message. Dead-letter msg-895290 and add a retry limit. Red herrings: line 200 (a single long GC pause in a healthy service, with heap well below limits); line 207 (a client sending one invalid request, rejected correctly with a 400); line 34 (a routine disk usage warning on the log volume, nowhere near full); line 199 (a one-off slow reporting query on audit_log, not on the failing request path).
